passages.original: De natura cæli, quod non sit ex quatuor elementis secundum Aristotelem.
passages.english: On the nature of the heaven: that it is not [made] of the four elements, according to Aristotle.

passages.original: Nunc autem non est unum quod sanat, sed multa; minime ergo ex uno elemento constituitur homo. Cæterum ex quibus ipsi conantur proprium quisque communire dogma, his maxime ostenditur quatuor esse elementa; etenim Thales aquam solam dicens elementum, demonstrare nititur reliqua tria ab hac generari, nam hypostasim ejus terram fieri quod λεπτομερέστερον est, aerem, quod tenuius autem aere, ignem. Anaximenes vero aerem solum ponens, oslendere quoque tentat alia elementa ex aere produci.
passages.english: But as it is, what heals is not one thing but many; therefore man is by no means constituted from a single element. Moreover, the very [arguments] from which each of them tries to strengthen his own doctrine show most clearly that there are four elements. For Thales, saying that water alone is an element, strives to demonstrate that the other three are generated from it: for its sediment becomes earth; what is finer [than water], air; and what is thinner than air, fire. Anaximenes, positing air alone, likewise tries to show that the other elements are produced from air.
passages.notes: "hypostasim" here appears to mean the sediment or settled residue of water. The Greek λεπτομερέστερον ("of finer parts") is left in Greek in the Latin; I have rendered it as "finer [than water]". The comparison "than water" is only implied. "oslendere" is read as "ostendere" (scanning error).
